Q: multiple threads write on common flag A:

I recommend that you use atomic_flag or atomic_bool as the data type for flag_failed. In that case, you do not need a mutex, and one flag for all threads is sufficient. You should not use a non-atomic type, because this will invoke undefined behavior if more than one thread writes to the flag. For example, a torn write is possible (but on most platforms will not occur for such small data types, and even if a torn write does occur, will likely not have any consequences for a simple flag variable).

However, if you have many threads setting this flag many times per thread, then this will be bad for performance, because the cache coherency protocol will be doing a lot of work, because the cache line with the flag will be transferring ownership to different CPUs many times. In that case, it would probably be better to have one flag per thread. These flags should not be adjacent in memory, but should be on different cache lines (for example by making them at least 64 bytes apart on x86-64 CPUs) in order to prevent false sharing.

Using atomic_flag instead of atomic_bool has the advantage that it is guaranteed to be lock-free. However, the disadvantage is that you cannot set it directly, but must use atomic_flag_test_and_set and atomic_flag_clear.

But on most common platforms, you can rely on atomic_bool being lock-free too, even if this is not guaranteed by the standard.
